title: Under true concurrency, a stale --if-revision with a gone removal target still exits 6, not 5
description: Reported by lore-cli 2026-09-27 and filed on opum-agent's instruction, targeted at the NEXT pair version, not 0.11.0 (ruling: v0.11.0 at eb1d9f4 stands, and lore LCLI-614 absorbs this for the pair). MEASURED by lore-cli against the v0.11.0 darwin-arm64 build (run 36285769701, sha256 d6a10b42). SERIAL: quest task edit <id> --remove-label x --if-revision <stale> after a competing removal exits 5 conflict (the QCLI-374 fix, also measured here, where 0.10.0 exits 6). CONCURRENT: lore unlink and a competing `quest task edit <id> --remove-label doc:<sid>` fired together. lore's argv was `task edit T-1 --actor-kind human --remove-label doc:stories/race-N --if-revision <rev read before the competitor> --json`, and it got `--remove-label: no entry matches` (validation, exit 6) in 3 of 3 manual trials. The opum-cli-e2e TASK-90 row is red 5/5 against lore c9b9377e. MECHANISM NOT YET IDENTIFIED, stated plainly: in src/cli/commands/task/index.ts the edit path reads one snapshot (prepareMutation), checks --if-revision against it (QCLI-374), builds the patch from that same snapshot, and TaskService.editOn writes with expectedRevision = snapshot.revision (src/application/tasks/tasks.ts ~1080). So a competitor committing between the read and the write should surface as a write conflict. Where the post-competitor state reaches the value check is the first thing to find: a retry or rebase in the repository write path, a revision that does not change on a label-only write, or a second read. lore-cli offered its race.sh repro. Impact: a caller that retries only on exit 5, as quest's own agent contract prescribes, cannot absorb a lost race.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The mechanism is named from evidence: the code path through which a concurrent competitor's write reaches the removal value check despite a stale --if-revision
Under a real concurrent competitor, a stale --if-revision with a gone removal target exits 5 conflict, proven by a concurrency test that fails on the 0.11.0 code and passes after the fix
A current (non-stale) --if-revision with a genuinely absent target still exits 6, so the fix does not turn real misses into conflicts
opum-cli-e2e's TASK-90 row passes against this quest with a lore that does not rely on the LCLI-614 re-read
